newsitem.title: USA: Teen indicted in bomb threat against Florida school.
newsitem.headline: Teen indicted in bomb threat against Florida school.

text.p: A federal grand jury has indicted a student for threatening to blow up a building and kill a professor at a Florida university campus, U.S. authorities said Tuesday.
The indictment was issued five months after the University of South Florida was shut for a day by a threat made in a letter to the school newspaper that sparked fears of Islamic terrorism on campus.

Damian Conrad Hospital, 19, a USF student, was charged with two counts of mailing threatening communications and faced a possible 10-year prison term and $500,000 fine if convicted, said Assistant U.S. Attorney Mac Cauley.
"The indictment alleges that he sent a letter in the mail to USF threatening to blow up a building on campus and threatening to kill a female professor," Cauley said.
A letter by an anonymous author, sent March 25 and printed in the newspaper The Oracle, promised to set off a bomb and to kill a white, female professor April 29.
The letter, signed by "The One, the War Purgers," triggered a massive security operation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and campus police.

Officials said the letter was taken seriously because it demanded an apology for what it called slanderous media treatment of former USF Professor Ramadan Abdullah Shallah, who surfaced in Syria last year as the leader of Islamic Jihad, an anti-Israeli fundamentalist group.
Due to the threat the school moved up final exams one week so students could move out of dorms before the specified date.
Cauley said he could not comment on whether Hospital was linked to any Islamic fundmentalist groups or whether the threat might have been a college prank.
